rfm_tuples.R: The net interest margin decreased to 2.69% for the year ended September 30, 2024, from 3.40% for the year ended September 30, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify NIM decline trajectory via FDIC Call Reports for WaFd Bank (CERT 28088); test whether the disclosed FY24 figure understates the quarterly run-rate going into Q2 FY25.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FDIC NIMY for WaFd Bank (CERT 28088): 3.46% (Mar-23), 3.37% (Jun-23), 3.31% (Sep-23), 3.21% (Dec-23), 2.61% (Mar-24, LBC close), 2.71% (Jun-24), 2.72% (Sep-24), 2.65% (Dec-24), 2.55% (Mar-25). 10-K-reported FY24 GAAP NIM (2.69%) reconciles to Call Report quarters. Q2 FY25 10-Q discloses 2.55% — still compressing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Claim is accurate but understated by the timing — by the cutoff 10-Q (Mar-25) NIM was 2.55%, a further 14bp slip below FY24, and 91bp cumulative below pre-merger peak. The 10-K narrative does not foreshadow continued compression.

rfm_tuples.R: On February 29, 2024, WaFd, Inc. closed its merger with Luther Burbank Corporation ... The Merger added approximately $7.7 billion of LBC assets at fair value ... and the Company assumed $50,175,000 in floating rate junior subordinated debentures, due June 2036 and June 2037, and $93,514,000 in 6.5% senior unsecured term notes which matured and were paid off on September 30, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify (a) LBC merger registration (S-4) and EDGAR-filed merger 8-Ks; (b) post-merger goodwill and asset additions; (c) whether the disclosed asset add reconciles to the balance-sheet jump.
rfm_tuples.M_value: EDGAR FTS returns LBC merger 8-K (acc 0001475348-24-000004 filed 2024-01-30) and WaFd 8-K/A 2024-02-20 (acc 0000936528-24-000051) confirming close. 10-K XBRL: Goodwill rose $304.75M -> $411.36M (+$106.6M); Total deposits $16.07B -> $21.37B (+$5.3B, consistent with LBC's $5B-ish deposit book); Loans $17.48B -> $20.92B (+$3.4B). FDIC asset jump Mar-23 $22.3B -> Mar-24 $30.1B (LBC consolidation).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Merger close and balance-sheet impact verified across EDGAR + FDIC + XBRL. No discrepancy.

rfm_tuples.R: Customer accounts with uninsured or uncollateralized deposits totaled $5,134,192,000 as of September 30, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Compare to total deposits to derive uninsured-deposit ratio; benchmark vs the canonical regional-bank uninsured-pct stress trigger (>40%); cross-check FDIC DEPDOM trend for deposit-run signature in 2024-2025.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Uninsured $5.13B / total deposits $21.37B = 24.0% — below the 30%+ flag threshold that triggered SVB/SBNY/FRC runs in 2023. FDIC DEPDOM trajectory: $21.54B (Jun-24), $21.52B (Sep-24), $21.57B (Dec-24), $21.59B (Mar-25) — flat, no run signature. Deposit composition stable through the cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Uninsured ratio is modest for a regional bank and deposit base is stable. Not a Silicon Valley-style risk; capital structure looks adequately funded.

rfm_tuples.R: WAFD's credit risks remain lower than average ... exposure to the troubled office sector is well-contained at just 4% of loans (KBRA, August 22, 2024, filed as Ex-99.3 to 8-K 0000936528-24-000117).
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check the office-exposure claim by reading the FY24 10-K loan-portfolio segment XBRL and quarterly Call Report CRE breakdowns; verify the disclosed CRE/multifamily/residential mix.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 loan mix per XBRL: SFR + Multifamily $13.13B (58.7%); Commercial $8.40B (37.6%); HELOC $384M (1.7%); Construction custom $672M (3.4%); Land $109M (0.5%); HEL $126M (0.6%); Consumer-other $266M (1.2%). Multifamily $5.36B (LBC-acquired) is the largest CRE-type sub-bucket; pure-office is not separately broken out in 10-K but KBRA's 4% figure is consistent with the 'Commercial' bucket being mostly C&I + owner-occupied, not investor office. 10-K Risk Factors do flag CRE concentration but do not quantify office.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Office concentration not separately disclosed in 10-K XBRL — relying on KBRA's 4% figure. CRE/multifamily concentration grew materially via LBC merger (multifamily-heavy California portfolio); the 10-K could have been more transparent about office vs other-CRE split. Not red-flag but a disclosure-quality miss.

rfm_tuples.R: Total non-accrual loans were $69.54 million (0.33% of total loans) at September 30, 2024, vs $50.42 million (0.29%) at September 30, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify trajectory via (a) FDIC NCLNLS quarterly series for CERT 28088 and (b) Q2 FY25 10-Q disclosure of non-accruals at 2025-03-31.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FDIC NCLNLS: Mar-23 $35.4M, Sep-23 $50.4M, Dec-23 $45.3M, Mar-24 $60.8M, Jun-24 $62.3M, Sep-24 $69.5M (matches 10-K), Dec-24 $72.5M, Mar-25 $59.9M. Q2 FY25 10-Q confirms non-accrual loans declined to $59.89M (0.28%) at Mar-31-2025. So non-accruals PEAKED in Q1 calendar 2025 and improved post-cutoff snapshot.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Non-accrual level is low (sub-0.35%) and reversed in the cutoff quarter. Credit quality is benign by Call Report data and matches the 10-K narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: Net charge-offs for fiscal 2024 were $9.31 million (vs $8.64M in fiscal 2023), and the provision for credit losses was $17.5 million (vs $41.5M in fiscal 2023).
rfm_tuples.f: Verify charge-off level via FDIC NTLNLS ytd; check whether the provision drop is justified by the loss experience or is a reserve-release earnings-management flag.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FDIC NTLNLS (ytd Call Report) shows very low charge-offs in CY2024: $146K Mar-24, $1.4M Jun-24, $1.5M Sep-24, $1.7M Dec-24 (ytd). ACL $/loans: $203.75M / $20.92B = 0.97% at Sep-30-2024, vs $177.21M / $17.48B = 1.01% at Sep-30-2023. ACL ratio held roughly steady; the lower provision is principally because the prior-year provision included a CECL Day-1 reserve build for LBC-acquired loans. The 'Day-1' build is disclosed in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Reserve coverage held near 1% of loans through merger integration. No evidence of provision under-accrual to flatter EPS.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company ... has paid 166 consecutive quarterly cash dividends and has returned 15,195% total shareholder return to those who invested 42 years ago.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify dividend continuity via 8-K dividend-declaration filings and DEF14A historical pattern; check pre-cutoff dividend declarations.
rfm_tuples.M_value: EDGAR submissions show recurring 7.01 / 8.01 Item dividend-declaration 8-Ks through 2025-04-15 (acc 0000936528-25-000061) and 2025-05-05 (acc 0000936528-25-000066). Pre-cutoff cadence is continuous. Most recent declaration before cutoff is the April-2025 8-K. Series A preferred dividend continues per 8-K filings.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend-streak claim verified through EDGAR. Capital return discipline intact.

rfm_tuples.R: Bank capital ratios are well above 'well capitalized' thresholds: Total Capital to RWA 14.29% (FY24) vs 13.31% (FY23) — bank-level (filing reports holding-company and bank-level separately).
rfm_tuples.f: Verify capital ratios against Call Report and against the 10% 'well-capitalized' regulatory threshold.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K XBRL + FDIC implicit (via Call Reports' regulatory capital section)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K XBRL: us-gaap:CapitalToRiskWeightedAssets values include 14.29%, 14.08%, 13.31%, 12.81% — all above 10% 'well capitalized' threshold and above 8% adequacy threshold. Capital absolute levels (~$2.72B for FY24 bank) reconcile to deposits/loan growth from LBC merger. ROA per Call Report trended 1.21% (Mar-23) -> 0.84% (Mar-25), still positive in every quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital adequacy is genuine; no evidence of distress. Earnings power has compressed but absolute ROA still 0.7-0.9%.

rfm_tuples.M_value: auditor_change_tracker(cik=0000936528, lookback=5y, cutoff=2025-05-15) returns signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE, 0 Item 4.01 filings, 0 disagreements. 31 8-K filings in 2024-2025 reviewed for items — none carry Item 4.01 or Item 4.02. rfm_tuples.R: [Implied] Senior management continuity and confidence in the integrated franchise post-LBC merger. The 10-K does not flag any executive departures.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: scan pre-cutoff 8-K Item 5.02 filings (officer departures / compensation arrangements) for any executive-level transition that the 10-K narrative did not foreshadow.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar (8-K Item 5.02 review) + form4 insider activity
rfm_tuples.M_value: 8-K Item 5.02 filed 2025-01-21 (acc 0000936528-25-000031): EVP & Chief Commercial Banker James Endrizzi was DEMOTED from executive officer to SVP Regional Director for CRE in UT/ID, effective 2025-01-16 — i.e., AFTER the 10-K but BEFORE the cutoff. Per Transition Agreement he forfeited 37,841 unvested restricted-stock / performance shares, his FY25 short-term incentive, and his Change-in-Control Agreement was terminated. Insider Form-4 review (12mo pre-cutoff): total open-market insider sales just $1.05M (3 transactions), zero open-market buys, no clustered selling. The Chief Credit Officer (Mauer) sold $404K and Chief Consumer Banker (Cooper) sold $643K on routine schedules.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: the Chief Commercial Banker — the executive nominally accountable for the COMMERCIAL loan book that grew 30% (LBC merger) and now represents 37.6% of loans — was quietly stripped of executive-officer status and incentive participation 8 weeks after the 10-K, with full forfeiture of unvested awards. The 10-K offered no foreshadowing. This is a discretionary management decision adjacent to the franchise's largest integration risk; the partial 'demote-to-regional-director-of-CRE' framing in the Transition Agreement is unusually punitive (forfeiture + CiC termination). Insider trading volume is otherwise muted, so this is an internal-governance signal rather than a panic-sell signal.

supplemental_signals.insider_open_market_sales_12mo: $1.05M total, no clustered selling, no 10b5-1 abuse pattern
supplemental_signals.post_10K_governance_event: Chief Commercial Banker reassigned with full forfeiture (8-K 2025-01-21, Item 5.02) — Mode-B finding

summary: WAFD is a 108-year-old Pacific-Northwest thrift / community bank that absorbed Luther Burbank ($7.7B, primarily California multifamily) on 2024-03-01. The 10-K's core claims — NIM compression, low non-accruals, capital adequacy, dividend continuity, clean audit — all verify cleanly against FDIC Call Reports, EDGAR 8-K cadence, and XBRL. Two soft concerns surface only on Mode-B work: (1) office-vs-other-CRE concentration is not separately quantified in the 10-K XBRL (KBRA cites 4% office but the 10-K itself is silent), and (2) eight weeks after the 10-K filing, the Chief Commercial Banker was stripped of executive-officer status with full forfeiture of unvested equity, a punitive transition the 10-K did not foreshadow during an active merger-integration period for a commercial book that grew 30%. There is no going-concern, no auditor turnover, no insider distribution, no deposit-run signature. Earnings power has compressed (NIM 3.46% -> 2.55% over 8 quarters) but the franchise is not lying or obscuring distress.
